for the policy rate, inflation, and mortgage rules.

(דייר סרבן): a refusing owner, one who will not sell their rights for a Pinui Binui deal, or attaches unreasonable conditions, after the legal special majority of owners has agreed. A negotiated early-exit clause. Its actual wording determines when it can be used.

this page defines the Hebrew and technical terms you meet when you buy, finance, or check an Israeli property, grouped by where they come up. Each term gets one plain line. (תקן 21): the appraisers’ standard for testing whether a Pinui Binui project pays. A claim that an obligation has already been paid or otherwise discharged.
(תב”ע): a detailed plan, the legally binding document that sets land uses, building rights, the number of floors, site coverage and building lines for an area. Building under it still needs a permit.

the national land registry where ownership is recorded. See due diligence .
the national seismic-renewal framework whose expiry, local extensions and replacement arrangements require checking the actual area and application. See the TAMA 38 guide .
The national earthquake-strengthening framework. Check the current local route and the specific project’s rights and approvals.
The registered subparcel identifying a unit in a condominium.
An eligibility certificate specifying the approved assistance and conditions.
A named Housing Ministry assistance programme; its current availability and conditions require checking.
the occupancy permit that lets you legally move into a new build.
A commonly used name for the building’s utility-connection/occupancy approval. Check the actual approval and conditions.
the building committee that collects monthly fees and manages shared areas. See due diligence .

a short preliminary memo that can legally bind you. Do not sign one casually. See the buying process .
